verdict.rationale: RustDesk documents its remote-reach path: clients try peer-to-peer and fall back to a relay, which can be the public server or a self-hosted hbbs/hbbr server deployed via a compose file. A long-time user confirms reaching machines with their own relay and no port-opening or VPN, though other users report slow default servers and laggy connections even when self-hosted. missing for 10: documented port-forwarding requirements (which ports to open), first-party guidance for a VPN or direct-IP path, consistent hands-on reliability evidence for remote connections.

support.subject: As a power user, I can reach my machine away from home, with the relay, VPN, or port-forward path documented

citations.quote: Self-hosted ID/rendezvous and relay servers with Server OSS or Server Pro; clients connect peer to peer when they can and fall back to your relay.
Server OSS: a free, open-source ID/rendezvous server (hbbs) and relay server (hbbr) that you can deploy on your own infrastructure.
You can use our rendezvous/relay server, [set up your own](https://rustdesk.com/server), or [write your own rendezvous/relay server]
